contents.name: Definition 1.19 and (1.20)-(1.21): a bordism as a compact manifold with a partition of the boundary and two collar embeddings

Page 10 and Lemma 1.30: disjoint union passes to bordism classes and turns the set of classes into an abelian group with Y not Y null-bordant
Proposition 1.31: the zero-dimensional unoriented bordism group is Z/2 with generator the class of a point
Proposition 1.32, part: the real projective plane is not a boundary of a compact 3-manifold
Definition 1.29: restatement of commutative monoid and abelian group
Definition 1.33 and (1.35): Cartesian product and the ring structure on the bordism groups, with the point class as unit
Equation (1.41): Stiefel-Whitney numbers of a closed manifold, and their role in the oriented bordism discussion of Theorem 2.24
Equation (2.27): Pontryagin numbers as evaluated products of Pontryagin classes on the fundamental class
(2.16) Our first bordism invariant: the determinant-line self-intersection computes Omega_2 = Z/2
contents.reason: The pair does not build the determinant-line intersection invariant; the same non-bounding statement is proved here through Stiefel-Whitney numbers, and intersection-theoretic routes belong to the oriented/mod-two intersection-numbers pair.

contents.name: (2.23)-(2.24) Theorem 2.24: the oriented bordism ring, its rational generators CP^{2k}, two-torsion and the signature-theorem route
contents.reason: The rational and signature-theoretic structure of the oriented bordism ring belongs to the later characteristic-numbers and signature-theorem pairs and is not commissioned on this page.

contents.name: Proposition 1.32 remainder: Omega_1 = 0 and the Klein-bottle disk-bundle proof of Omega_2 = Z/2
contents.reason: The pair computes only the zero-dimensional groups; the higher bordism-group computations require the classification of surfaces and are not needed by any item of this pair.

contents.name: Section 4: definition of the Stiefel-Whitney number of a closed manifold associated with a monomial of total degree n
Section 4, page 51: for even n, w_1(TP^n) = a is nonzero and w_1^n[P^n] is nonzero
Theorem 4.9 with proof: all Stiefel-Whitney numbers of a boundary vanish, via the relative fundamental class and TB|_M = TM + epsilon^1
Theorem 4.10 (Thom): the converse that vanishing of all Stiefel-Whitney numbers forces bounding
contents.reason: The hard converse is the Thom detection theorem and belongs to the characteristic-numbers pair; this pair only proves the vanishing direction needed by its counterexample.

contents.name: Section 16: Chern numbers of compact complex manifolds
contents.reason: No complex manifold or Chern number is commissioned on this pair; the complex characteristic-class machinery is consumed only through the Pontryagin construction.

contents.name: Section 16: definition of the Pontryagin number p_{i_1}...p_{i_r}[M^{4n}] on the fundamental class
Section 16, printed pp.185-187: vanishing of Pontryagin numbers on an oriented boundary by the method of Section 4.9
Section 17, printed pp.199-200: manifolds with boundary, the boundary tangent hyperplane and the inward/outward normal splitting TB|_M = TM + epsilon^1
Section 17, Collar Neighborhood Theorem 17.1
Section 17: definition of oriented cobordism with the induced orientation of the boundary
Lemma 17.2: oriented cobordism is reflexive, symmetric and transitive
Section 17: the oriented cobordism classes form an abelian group and a graded ring under disjoint union and Cartesian product
Lemma 17.3 (Pontrjagin): every Pontryagin number of an oriented boundary vanishes
Corollaries 17.4-17.5: Pontryagin numbers are homomorphisms and products of CP^{2i} are linearly independent
contents.reason: The linear-independence computation uses Theorem 16.8 and the rational cohomology of the complex classifying space; it belongs to the later computation of the oriented bordism ring.

contents.name: Page 203: Omega_0 = Z, a compact oriented 0-manifold being a finite set of signed points with the signed sum complete
Page 203: the table of low-dimensional oriented bordism groups Omega_1,...,Omega_11

contents.name: Section 8.1, Propositions 8.1.1 and 8.1.4 and Theorem 8.1.3: the Thom construction bijections between cobordism classes of submanifolds and homotopy classes of maps
contents.reason: The general normal-structure-group Thom-bordism bijections are not commissioned by the selected collapse/preimage/homotopy/PD interface page. The framed subcase belongs to the future planned pontryagin-thom-and-framed-cobordism pair, but no already proved generic-J classification or exact future generic-J home is claimed.

contents.name: Section 8.1, Proposition 8.1.5: representing homology classes by oriented submanifolds and the Thom-class condition
contents.reason: The arbitrary-homology-class representability iff uses a universal SO Thom target and the full Thom-bordism bijection. The selected Thom page proves pullback-Poincare duality for a supplied submanifold only, without this converse; no exact existing adopted representability packet is asserted.

contents.name: Section 8.2: stable group axioms (S), (M), (A), (C), Lemma 8.2.6 and Corollary 8.2.8 on weak J-structures
contents.reason: This page defines geometric bordism groups without structure groups; the stable-group machinery exists to compare normal and tangent structures and is not consumed by any item here.

contents.name: Section 8.2, printed p.247: the natural abelian group structure by disjoint union and the inverse from the boundary of M x I
Section 8.2, printed pp.247-248: products are compatible with cobordism, Theorem 8.2.11 on the bilinear product and its associativity and graded commutativity
Section 8.2, Lemma 8.2.9 and Theorem 8.2.10: the bijection of cobordism groups with stable homotopy groups of the Thom spectrum T_J
contents.reason: The identification of geometric bordism groups with stable homotopy groups of a Thom spectrum requires the Pontrjagin-Thom construction and spectra, which are the subjects of the following two pairs and of algebraic topology.

contents.name: Section 8.2, Corollary 8.2.12: framed cobordism groups are the stable homotopy groups of spheres
contents.reason: Framed cobordism and its identification with stable homotopy groups of spheres are the subject of the Pontrjagin-Thom and framed-cobordism pair, not of this pair's group and ring laws.

contents.name: Section 8.2, printed p.246: tau W restricted to the boundary is tau(dW) + epsilon^1, with epsilon^1 identified with the inward normal on the incoming face and the outward normal on the outgoing face
Section 8.3, Lemma 8.3.1 and the corner-change technique: exact sequences of bordism groups
contents.reason: The exact-sequence techniques are tools for computing relative bordism groups and are not used by the definitions, group laws or boundary-vanishing results commissioned here.
